extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of chemistry; readers of physical-chemical reference tables (French)
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpt from a French chemistry reference/textbook providing tables of specific gravities for many substances and a descriptive table-of-contents-style treatment of acids (definitions, nomenclature, properties, methods of obtaining).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of specific gravities / weights (format and columns)
rubrics_metrics.description: TABLE des Pesanteurs spécifiques des Fluides. Columns: ESPECES / VARIÉTÉS; Pesant(e) spécifiq(ue); Poids du pouce cube; Poids du pied cube (values given in onces, grammes, grains, livres, onces, grammes, grains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every entry should list the species and variety, the specific gravity (pesanteur spécifique) and the corresponding weights expressed for a cubic inch (du pouce cube) and a cubic foot (du pied cube) using the same unit breakdown used in the table (onces, grammes, grains; liv., on., g., gr.). Examples in the text include categories such as EAUX, LIQUEURS SPIRITUEUSES, LIQUEURS ACIDES, Huiles, Résines, Gommes, Bois, etc., each with numeric specific gravities and computed weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: General definition of 'acids' (composition and formation)
rubrics_metrics.description: “ACIDES. Ils résultent en général d'un premier ordre de combinaisons formées par la réunion de deux principes simples, d'un radical particulier & d'un principe acidifiant commun à tous, l'oxigène.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize an acid by (1) its radical and (2) the common acidifying principle (oxygen). Note that acids are generally the result of combustion or oxygenation of a body; chemical descriptions should mention formation pathways and typical natural/industrial origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acid nomenclature rule (-eux vs -ique endings)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Leurs noms se terminent en _eux_ lorsqu'ils contiennent peu d'oxygène... Ils se terminent en _ique_, lorsqu'ils sont plus chargés de ce principe.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When naming acids in this system, use the ending -eux for less-oxygenated acids and -ique for more-oxygenated acids; relate the name to the name of the base (dénomination tirée de celle de leur base acidifiable). Record any exceptions or difficulties when the base is unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard contents of an acid entry (what to report)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each acid the text expects: 'Tableau de ses combinaisons, Moyens de l'obtenir, Ses propriétés & ses affinités, Solubilité/état, Radical composition, Occurrence.' (repeated across many acid headings: ex. Acide acétique, Acide carbonique, Acide fluorique, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full acid treatment should include a table of combinations (salts/compounds), methods to obtain the acid (procédés, voie sèche/voie humide), its properties (physical state, solubility, tendencies such as absorption of oxygen), affinities (what bases it combines with), and notes on natural occurrence. Also indicate if the radical composition is known or unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable chemical properties to record (examples from entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific notable properties mentioned include: Acide carbonique is widely present in nature, neutralized by lime, combines with water about equal by volume; Acide fluorique is naturally gaseous in fluor-spar and 'dissout le verre'; Acide acéteux (vinegar) forms by oxygenation of wine and absorbs oxygen from air while forming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting a substance or acid, record distinctive functional properties and hazards (e.g., glass-dissolving action of hydrofluoric species), typical formation/behavior (e.g., formation during combustion or fermentation), and any important practical notes (neutralization reactions, ease of obtaining, physical state under atmospheric pressure).
